KEY MESSAGE 1...Latest surface analysis shows previously 
mentioned warm front just off the coast this morning with 
isolated shower and thunderstorm activity riding SE'wards along
this front. A surface trough is also noted across the Triad 
vicinity which has produced some weakening showers and isolated 
tstms that are tracking west from central NC towards ENC this 
morning. While I have left PoPs sub mentionable this morning 
across the area, can't rule out a stray sprinkle mainly along 
northern portions of ENC before this aforementioned trough 
exits the region.

Overall the upper level pattern will remain the same in the
coming days with upper ridging settled into the Southeast 
promoting westerly flow into midweek before flow backs and 
becomes SW'rly later this week out ahead of an incoming upper 
level trough. At the mid levels, shortwave currently in the Mid-
Atlantic vicinity will push offshore this morning with next weak
shortwave not approaching the area until this evening. From Tue
onwards we likely see a series of weak shortwaves that track 
across the region and are diurnal in nature before the next 
significant shortwave approaches the region this weekend. 

Well what does this mean for us at ENC as far as ambient 
weather goes? Low level thicknesses across the region today 
increase to about 1435-1440+ m under westerly downslope flow. 
This westerly flow will pin the seabreeze closer to the coast 
today as a result. This will set the stage for highs in the mid 
to upper 90s inland with upper 80s to low 90s noted along the 
OBX. Any leftover debris clouds from overnight activity is 
forecast to quickly dissipate today allowing for mo clear skies 
into the afternoon. Current forecast reflects dewpoints in the 
mid to upper 70s inland and potentially nearing 80 behind the 
pinned seabreeze. There is some uncertainty with how much mixing
occurs today as W'rly downsloping flow does tend to mix us out 
more than forecast, but even then, the most aggressive guidance
only suggests dewpoints in the low 70s across the inner Coastal
Plain worst case. Regardless of mixing, with highs in the mid 
to upper 90s today, widespread heat indices of 105-110F are 
expected across ENC with the heat advisory remaining in place 
across Lenoir, Greene, Beaufort, Washington, Tyrrell, Dare, and
Hyde Counties. The one change I did make this forecast package 
was to upgrade portions of the heat advisory across Duplin, 
Onslow, Carteret, Craven, Jones, and Pamlico County to an 
extreme heat warning as heat indices look to get to about 
110-115F this afternoon. This area has the highest probability 
of reaching higher end heat impacts given its proximity to the
seabreeze and is supported by HREF probs around 40-60% of 
HI greater than 109F this afternoon. 

A weak frontal boundary quickly pushes across NC tonight before
stalling along the coast. Like this weekend, southern counties 
will likely remain hot and humid while Albemarle and vicinity 
see some modest relief. A more widespread cooldown, however, is 
on the horizon late week as a stronger cold front dives out of 
Canada and across the eastern CONUS. Overall, this just means 
additional heat headlines will be likely Tue/Wed/Thurs across 
at least portions of ENC before the second stronger front 
approaches Fri into this weekend.

mentioned warm front just off the coast this morning with 
isolated shower and thunderstorm activity riding SE'wards along
this front near the Albemarle Sound. A surface trough is also 
noted across the Triad vicinity which has produced some 
weakening showers and isolated tstms that are tracking west from
central NC towards ENC this morning.

Upper ridging is settled into the Southeast promoting westerly 
flow into midweek before flow backs and becomes SW'rly later 
this week out ahead of an incoming upper level trough. At the 
mid levels, shortwave currently in the Mid-Atlantic vicinity 
will push offshore this morning with next weak shortwave not 
approaching the area until this evening. 

A weakening cold front approaches from the north and west this 
evening. Aforementioned heat and humidity will easily boost 
instability with a forecast 2000-3000 J/kg of MLCAPE, but shear
will once again be lacking, generally 20 kt or less, and the 
next shortwave will not approach the area until later this 
evening. PWATs remain at or above 2" so conditions will once 
again be favorable for a stronger storm or two to impact the 
area bringing a damaging wind, frequent lightning, and 
torrential rain threat. We may see slightly less seabreeze 
activity today given westerly downslope flow with any precip 
today primarily coming from the incoming front this evening. 
Any upstream convection associated with this front will sweep 
E'wards this evening into ENC with the potential for some
